Comparing this label with the measured 10/1 midpoint c08c4700ae34281b3318, 21.70/47.67, tests whether the large completion increase persists in stronger eluent.

Measure m193 at 5/1 and 50 uL; prediction 10.17/30.56 mL. High boundary 0a79a24271d119590ae6 measured 11.71/31.07. The predicted low-amount onset is earlier than that measured high boundary, whereas the measured 20/1 panel has the opposite association. This tests contraction or reversal of the amount response, informed by m37's small measured 5/1 onset contrast in 4908bb1bf155952cd305 and 65f6e8326897810ec715.

Measure ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde m198 at 20/1 and 150 uL; prediction 23.99/51.79 mL. Low boundary cdaf95461fe3b3d80075 measured 27.33/54.16. The model predicts decreasing completion across these boundaries, unlike the newly measured para-isomer panel. This directly tests whether the completion response transfers across substitution environments under their respective catalog loading conditions.

Measure m198 at 10/1 and 150 uL; prediction 13.03/34.58 mL. Midpoint fcb9019ffbdb889489f7 measured 14.90/35.72. Together with the selected m198 20/1 boundary and m193 10/1 boundary, this connects amount responses across eluent strength and nitro substitution. Differences in density and loading-solvent volume prevent attributing the entire cross-molecule contrast to position alone.

Its 20/1 onset boundaries 2cf4f6424b85ab121943 and 80f6a235bb59c2a7ea59 differ by 11.64 mL, while its 5/1 boundaries 209cc7cf667dbec940db and cb6d3ef1b6dde291fbac differ by only 0.98. Completing the panel separates boundary amount contrast from an interior feature and may prevent an exceptional midpoint or an overly flat boundary response from propagating to related methyl-substituted acetophenones.

hypotheses.content: m193's measured 20/1 amount response combines earlier onset with substantially later completion. The onset association resembles m37, but completion does not transfer as a shared correction. Its solvent dependence and extension to ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde m198 remain unresolved; cross-isomer comparisons are conditional on their differing recorded loading conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest m193 high boundary exposed a roughly 20-mL completion underestimate despite a small onset error. Connected labels can teach endpoint-specific amount-by-eluent relationships without applying a nitroketone response indiscriminately to nitroaldehydes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m193's completion increase persist at 10/1 and contract at 5/1, and does m198 show the same completion-response sign at 20/1 and 10/1?

hypotheses.content: m67 has an eluent-dependent onset association with amount, with a large contrast in weak eluent and a small contrast at 5/1. Completion requires separate treatment: its new 20/1 midpoint completed below both measured boundaries. Whether the onset contrast contracts further at 2/1, and whether related m61 shares its response, remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These connected panels constrain amount invariance and endpoint coupling in an abundant alcohol motif. The m61 measurements test transfer while preserving within-molecule comparisons that hold its loading solvent fixed.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1, are m67's amount boundaries close together, and do m61's matched low-amount 2/1 and 5/1 labels support the predicted solvent ordering and its implied 5/1 amount association?

hypotheses.content: The model currently implies an interior onset minimum and completion maximum around m33's measured 50/1 midpoint, because both unmeasured amount boundaries are predicted later in V1 and earlier in V2. Neither feature is established by measured boundaries; boundary prediction error and variation unexplained by the inputs remain competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A complete local panel can distinguish useful amount curvature from propagation of an isolated midpoint or flattened boundary predictions. The aromatic methyl-ketone environment offers potential transfer to several related catalog molecules.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the 50- and 150-uL measurements resemble the predicted 13.6/34.3-mL boundaries, the measured 8.49/38.59-mL midpoint, or a response with different endpoint slopes?

hypotheses.content: m36's nearly amount-invariant 2/1 boundary predictions may conceal a real amount response or a shared endpoint underestimate. Their being below the single measured midpoint does not establish a midpoint maximum. Silica interactions provide a prior for loading sensitivity, but its sign and endpoint dependence must be measured for this aminoaryl ketone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The pair adds direct constraints in a nitrogen environment currently represented at this ratio by one midpoint. It can prevent borrowing amount-response magnitude or shape from aminoesters, aminonitriles or nonbasic carbonyl compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the low and high boundaries show an onset contrast, and does completion change in the same direction, remain similar or form an interior elevation?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest m193 panel changes the priority most strongly. From low to high amount at 20/1, onset fell by 7.45 mL while completion rose by 19.72 mL. The earlier-onset extension from m37 is supported, but a small or shared completion correction is not. m37's measured 5/1 onset contrast was only 1.60 mL, supporting eluent-dependent contraction. I therefore extend the nitroaldehyde experiment across ratios and compare the ortho analogue without assuming identical loading conditions.

The m67 20/1 midpoint onset, 34.61 mL, lay between its boundaries, but completion, 59.42 mL, was below both boundary values near 62–63 mL. Thus nearly stable boundary completion does not establish a flat full response. The m94 midpoint, 37.25/79.67, interpolated within both boundary ranges, and m25's 5/1 boundaries differed only modestly. These outcomes support conditional amount responses while discouraging a universal curve across esters or alcohols. The recent CW m61 2/1 high boundary, 11.82/21.78, also exposed substantial underprediction and motivates a connected alcohol comparison.

m160's 5/1 midpoint interpolated between its boundaries. At matched 1/1 high loading, para and meta aminobenzonitriles differed by only 0.40 mL in onset and 0.56 mL in completion, supporting contraction of their weak-eluent gap. m90's new 2/1 low-to-midpoint comparison showed a 2.48-mL onset decline with almost unchanged completion. These questions now have useful anchors, so they receive no further supplements here. The m128 midpoint lay between its measured onset boundaries, rejecting its predicted below-boundary onset; this informs the independent m31 interpolation test.

The neighboring-eluent m207 midpoint outcomes, 10.52/17.58 at 2/1 and 38.08/66.27 at 10/1, do not support an exceptionally early response at 100 uL across ratios. Its unusual 5/1 midpoint remains localized or unexplained by supplied inputs. The m92 repeats further weaken deterministic interior-shape claims: repeated low-boundary completions moved from 21.03 to 26.35 at 10/1 and from 52.44 to 58.54 at 50/1, closer to their midpoint ranges. I pause expansion of those shapes. The m27 neat-EA and m45 1/1 labels also rejected their predicted strong-eluent completion increases and now provide terminal anchors. All error statements refer to acquisition-time predictions, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The sixteen supplements are distinct eligible candidate IDs with no overlap with the pending sixteen. Together they form the frozen 32-experiment batch, retaining the supplied full-precision premeasurement predictions; numbers in the reasons are rounded only for readability.

The pending batch supplies many ordinary-condition coverage points. The supplements emphasize relationships that isolated points cannot resolve. Four nitroaldehyde labels investigate the largest new completion failure and whether its response depends on eluent strength and substitution environment. Four alcohol labels connect a recent CW failure to measured amount panels and test a predicted solvent ordering. The m36 and m33 boundary pairs independently discriminate prediction-implied interior features from boundary error. These repeated-molecule choices have specific local experimental roles rather than serving diversity quotas.

The remaining four labels broaden the learning questions: m31 checks an endpoint prediction outside measured boundary ranges; m159 tests an uncovered amount boundary in another cyanoaryl carbonyl environment; m169 anchors separate onset and completion solvent responses; and m167 tests where a fluorinated beta-diketone structural contrast appears. These comparisons may improve generalization across common alcohol, nitrogen-containing aromatic and carbonyl rows while limiting unsupported transfer between related compounds.

The latest repeated-input disagreements argue for caution about deterministic mechanisms and reduce the value of further expanding m92's apparent extrema this round. Within-molecule comparisons hold the other recorded conditions fixed where stated; cross-molecule contrasts can remain confounded by density, loading solvent and its volume. Density times sample volume is the recorded amount feature, so the experiments establish conditional associations rather than a loading mechanism. Quantile spans are single-predictor outputs, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 remains the elution interval width.
